entries.02997e1a12d49fa0: The main customers of the Wealth Management Division are individual investors in Japan and unlisted companies. The main customers of Global Markets are domestic and overseas institutional investors, business corporations, financial institutions, public corporations and others, and those of the Asset Management Division are domestic and overseas institutional investors. The number of bank accounts at Daiwa Next Bank increased 20.8% year on year to 2.28 million accounts. Net operating revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026, broken down by customer location, was ¥625,322 million in Japan, ¥48,651 million in Europe, ¥28,510 million in Asia and Oceania, and ¥17,941 million in the United States. No counterparty accounts for 10% or more of net operating revenue.

entries.4c6804065f1f572b: This is a [[term:holding-company|holding company]] whose purpose is to control and manage group companies. The principal business of its 138 consolidated subsidiaries and 39 equity-method affiliates is investment and financial services centered on securities-related business. Domestic and overseas strategies are set by management organizations based on customer markets and business types, and [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]] such as Daiwa Securities Co. Ltd., Daiwa Asset Management Co. Ltd., Daiwa Next Bank, Ltd. and Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd. carry out the businesses. The company has business bases in major financial markets in Japan, Europe, Asia and the Americas.
entries.4d1ce091c604992c: This division sets up and manages investment trusts that invest in a variety of assets, and provides investment advisory and asset management services to institutional investors in Japan and overseas. It also manages investment corporations and funds that invest in real estate, and invests in assets such as monetary claims, private equity, venture capital, real estate, renewable energy and infrastructure. Net operating revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 is ¥134,912 million.

entries.53c637455fbc947b: The Wealth Management Division provides a broad range of financial products and services mainly to individuals and unlisted corporations. The Asset Management Division establishes and manages investment trusts, provides investment advisory and management services to domestic and overseas institutional investors, and manages investment corporations and funds investing in real estate, and also invests in monetary claims, private equity, venture capital, real estate, renewable energy, infrastructure and others. The Global Markets & Investment Banking Division conducts sales and trading of equities, bonds and foreign exchange and their derivatives, underwriting of securities, M&A advisory and others. The reportable [[term:segment|segments]] are these three; the integration and management of subsidiaries, information services, clerical services, real estate leasing and others are included in 'Other'.

entries.85e5f50c6f249692: Operating revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1.4679 trillion, up 7.0% year on year, and net operating revenue was ¥720.4 billion, up 11.5% year on year. Commissions received were ¥478.4 billion, up 14.9% year on year; brokerage commissions rose 23.2% to ¥109.6 billion owing to increased equity trading, and fees for underwriting, secondary offerings and solicitation of sales to specified investors fell 16.7% to ¥39.9 billion owing to fewer equity underwriting deals. Net operating revenue from external customers was ¥278,025 million for the Wealth Management Division, ¥255,511 million for the Global Markets & Investment Banking Division, ¥134,912 million for the Asset Management Division, and ¥15,226 million for Other. The main sources of revenue by division are: for Wealth Management, fees on products and services relating to asset management and administration for individuals and unlisted companies, and net interest margin income from Daiwa Next Bank; for Global Markets, customer flow income and trading income; and for Investment Banking, underwriting and secondary offering fees and M&A fees. Asset Management earns revenue from investment trust management fees, real estate operating income, gains on sale of investees, management fees, dividends, electricity sales income and others.

entries.b12129bdeabcaaa7: Under the group medium-term management plan 'Passion for the Best 2026', covering fiscal 2024 to fiscal 2026, the group's basic management policy is 'Maximizing Customers' Asset Value'. In fiscal 2025, the second year of the medium-term plan, the company strengthened its wealth management business and advanced its asset management business, and implemented an inorganic strategy aimed at expanding its customer base and strengthening solution functions and product lineup. In fiscal 2026, the final year of the plan, the Wealth Management, Asset Management and Global Markets & Investment Banking divisions and the Daiwa Institute of Research Group have each set action plans.
